Bill Clinton, there was an attempt to gin up anti-government sentiment, like, you know, you scapegoat government for whatever you don't like that's going on, a lot of, anticipation of what we saw later with the Tea Party, and even with Donald Trump. I mean, this kind of right-wing push in our politics has been with us for a long time. We need a conservative force in politics. We need a center-right to Republican Party, just like we need a center-left Democratic Party. But the American system works best when both parties are big tents. You know, we don't have a parliamentary system. If you have a different party in the presidency and the Congress, you're going to have to come together or the government's going to shut down. And so we have a system that historically has depended on, yes, vigorous politics. Nobody questions that or should question it. But at the end of the day, there needs to be an ability to come together and to articulate some kind of version of the common good that at least keeps us together until we can have the next round of political contests. And that capacity I worry is is in some jeopardy. I just appalled about what happened on January 6th here with the capital being stormed with a certain number of members, way too many members saying they aren't going to certify a legitimate election and a sitting president trying not to leave office, trying not to engage in the peaceful transition apart. Who ever thought this country would see that? So I do think there's some earlier hints of the divisions and the extremism that was to come. But I do think recent months have broken some new ground, unfortunately, and given us some new things to be concerned about. All that by way of saying, I guess, that I'm not leaving with any sense of complacency. It has been a wonderful opportunity. I never dreamed I would do this let alone stay 30 plus years. So I'm so grateful for that. But I also welcome the opportunity to use the time I have left to try to make some headway and also to issue some very serious thoughts and warnings about where our democracy needs to head and how we need to protect it.
